key_insight: A new finite-volume convolution unit lets CNN super-resolution work directly on non-uniform, non-orthogonal meshes by replacing standard grid-based convolutions with finite-volume operators.
engineering_relevance: This makes turbulence reconstruction methods usable on the kinds of meshes actually employed in wall-bounded and complex-geometry CFD simulations.
method: Builds convolution from exact axis-wise decompositions of 3D convolution
Uses finite-volume gradient, averaging, and identity operators so layers work on arbitrary polyhedral cells
Adds Van Driest damping as a wall-proximity conditioning input
evidence_signal: The model was trained and evaluated on 4× coarsened channel-flow and pipe-flow data, accurately recovering velocity fields, Reynolds stresses, anisotropy, and energy spectra beyond the coarse-grid Nyquist limit, with additional tests on an unseen elliptic pipe.
watch_item: Performance is slightly weaker on the unseen elliptic pipe, with modest overprediction of small-scale energy, so generalization to new geometries and mesh types still needs careful validation.
paper_title: Extending convolutional neural networks to finite-volume meshes for fine-scale reconstruction of wall-bounded turbulence
